sections.title: A European Education of Exceptional Value
sections.intro: Poland has emerged as one of Europe’s most compelling study destinations, combining recognised European qualifications with remarkably accessible costs.

items.title: Europe-wide recognition
items.desc: Degrees follow the European Higher Education Area framework, supporting recognition and mobility across Europe.

items.title: Exceptional affordability
items.desc: Tuition and living costs are among the lowest in the European Union, allowing students to invest in quality education with confidence.

items.title: Strong academic and career fields
items.desc: Poland is distinguished in medicine, engineering, information technology, business and finance, with a thriving technology and services economy.

items.title: A European gateway
items.desc: As a member of the Schengen Area, Poland places much of Europe within easy reach for study, travel and work.

items.title: A vibrant student environment
items.desc: From the energy of Warsaw to the historic student life of Kraków, Wrocław and Poznań, Polish cities are safe, modern and welcoming.

sections.title: Leading Polish Universities
sections.intro: The following institutions represent key destinations available to EUROPA FUSION students.

items.name: University of Warsaw
items.desc: Poland’s leading comprehensive university, with strengths across the sciences, law, economics, humanities and social sciences.

items.name: Jagiellonian University
items.desc: A major historic research university with distinguished programmes in medicine, sciences, humanities and law.

items.name: Warsaw University of Technology
items.desc: A leading centre for engineering, information technology, architecture and applied sciences.

items.name: AGH University of Krakow
items.desc: Renowned for engineering, computer science, energy and materials, with strong industry cooperation.

items.name: Wrocław University of Science and Technology
items.desc: Known for engineering, architecture and technology, with a large and growing international community.

items.name: Adam Mickiewicz University
items.desc: A comprehensive university recognised for the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences and modern languages.

items.name: SGH Warsaw School of Economics
items.desc: A leading Polish institution for economics, finance, management, international business and quantitative analytics.

items.name: Medical University of Warsaw
items.desc: A specialist institution offering English-taught programmes in medicine (6-year MD), dentistry, pharmacy and health sciences.

sections.title: From Enquiry to Enrolment
sections.intro: EUROPA FUSION offers a structured, transparent process so that each stage is handled with care and precision.

items.title: Profile evaluation
items.desc: Academic record, career goals, budget and preferred city are reviewed to define a realistic shortlist.

items.title: Programme & university selection
items.desc: Courses are matched to your profile, with attention to language of instruction, entry tests and deadlines.

items.title: Application to the university
items.desc: Transcripts, certificates, language proof, CV, motivation letter and passport are prepared and submitted directly.

items.title: Entrance assessment
items.desc: Where required, preparation for entrance examinations or interviews, for example for medical and technical programmes.

items.title: Admission & tuition confirmation
items.desc: Acceptance of your offer, issue of the official admission letter and payment of the first instalment of tuition.

items.title: Student visa (Type D)
items.desc: Preparation of the national visa file, including proof of funds, accommodation evidence and compliant health insurance.

items.title: Arrival & residence permit
items.desc: Application for the temporary residence permit (Karta Pobytu) before visa expiry, followed by accommodation and orientation.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Common questions about studying and settling in Poland.

items.q: Can I study in Poland entirely in English?
items.a: Yes. Polish universities offer a large and growing selection of English-taught programmes at Bachelor’s, Master’s and doctoral level, including medicine and dentistry.

items.q: Do I need to speak Polish?
items.a: It is not required for English-taught programmes, but basic Polish is very helpful for daily life, part-time work and career prospects. Polish-taught programmes require certified proficiency, typically at B2 level.

items.q: How much does it cost to study in Poland?
items.a: Poland is one of Europe’s most affordable destinations. Tuition for non-medical programmes is commonly in the range of €2,000 to €6,000 per year, while medical programmes cost considerably more (€9,500–€13,000/yr). Monthly living costs typically range from €400 to €800.

items.q: When are the intakes and deadlines?
items.a: The main intake begins in October, with a smaller intake in February or March at some universities. Many institutions admit on a rolling basis, though earlier application improves visa timing. Begin preparing at least 6 to 9 months in advance.

items.q: Do I need to take an entrance examination?
items.a: Most Bachelor’s and Master’s programmes assess applicants on their academic record and a motivation letter. Medicine, dentistry and certain other programmes require entrance examinations or interviews.
Universities usually accept IELTS, TOEFL or an equivalent, and some conduct their own interview or test. Requirements differ by institution.

items.q: How much money must I show for the student visa?
items.a: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for their stay. In practice consulates and universities expect proof of around €3,500 to €7,000 for the first year, often alongside payment of the first tuition instalment.

items.q: Can I work while studying in Poland?
items.a: Full-time students at accredited Polish institutions may generally work part-time without a separate work permit during their studies. You should always maintain academic attendance as priority.

items.q: Can I remain in Poland after graduating?
items.a: Graduates may apply for a temporary residence permit to look for work or start a business, for a period set by current regulations (typically 9-12 months), and may then transition to a full work permit or Blue Card.

items.q: Are scholarships available for international students?
items.a: Yes. Options include NAWA programmes (e.g. Banach or Gen. Anders), Erasmus+, and merit-based fee reductions from individual universities. Competition is strong and deadlines are early.
Students may choose university dormitories, which are typically the most economical option (PLN 480 to PLN 1,100 / month, approx €110–€250), or private shared rentals in Warsaw, Kraków and Wrocław.

Typically: passport, academic transcripts and certificates (with apostille/legalisation and sworn translation if needed), language-test results, CV, motivation letter, proof of financial means, proof of accommodation and health insurance.

items.q: How does EUROPA FUSION support my application?
items.a: We assist at every stage: profile assessment, university selection, application and document preparation, scholarship guidance, visa support, accommodation and pre-departure briefing.
